newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares mixed in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares mixed in dull trade.

text.p: Lithuanian shares were mixed in dull trade on Monday but dealers said that prices seemed set to stabilise soon as sellers dig in and refuse to part with their shares at current prices.
"Sellers seem to be reluctant to sell at such low prices...if the situation continues, the market should soon stabilise," said Arvydas Jacikevicius of brokerage house Suprema.
Demand for equities remained low on Monday and dealers said that foreign portfolio investors, whose concerns about the government's monetary policies have eased, seemed more interested in debt.
Yields have been falling steadily at primary auctions for Lithuanian Treasury bills as foreigners have returned to the market, driving up demand, dealers said.
On the equities market, Birzai Dairy was in relative demand in trade of just over 109,000 litas at the unchanged price of 10.25 litas.
The session's few big gainers included cardboard maker Medienos Plaushas, which rose to 12.99 litas from 12.00 litas in trade of only 4,500 litas.
Dealers said that the company seemed to be a bit underpriced but were unsure if it would rise much more in the current climate.
There were no really big price movements in the banking sector and banking shares only turned over 48,380 litas.
